svg.text: BEST FOR: EVALS THAT START FROM REAL TRACES
FORMAT LINEAGE: Hamel Husain & Shreya Shankar, AI Evals method
Stop Guessing Why Your Agent Fails: Read 100 Traces, Build a Taxonomy, Then Write the Judge
The error-analysis method Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar teach: look at the data first; evals come out of it, not the other way round. Example run on a support agent.
STEP 1 • READ 100 REAL TRACES AND WRITE WHAT WENT WRONG (OPEN CODING)
trace #0412 • 'Refund order 88213, I was charged twice'
Issued one refund, never checked the duplicate charge.
Said 'done' — no tool call was made.
Called get_order with the wrong ID (88970).
Pasted raw JSON in the reply.
STEP 2 • GROUP NOTES INTO A FAILURE TAXONOMY (AXIAL CODING)
Right intent, wrong call: bad ID, wrong tool, missing
The answer is plausible but violates something the user
example: refund to store credit, not the card
Claims an action happened; no tool call exists in the
Loops on clarifying questions when it already has enough
example: raw JSON in a customer reply
STEP 3 • PARETO: WHICH FAILURES ARE WORTH FIXING FIRST?
Two failure modes explain 59% of failures — fix those first; the long tail can wait.
STEP 4 • ONE BINARY JUDGE PER TOP FAILURE MODE
You are grading ONE failure mode only: 'Fabricated a tool result'. Read
the trace. Did the assistant claim an action (refund, change, send) that
has no matching tool call in the trace? Answer PASS if no fabricated
claims, FAIL otherwise. Then give one sentence of evidence quoting the
STEP 5 • CHECK THE JUDGE AGAINST HUMANS BEFORE TRUSTING IT
Label 40 held-out traces by hand. Run the judge. Require TPR >= 0.90 and TNR
>= 0.90 before using it on thousands of traces; recheck after every prompt
WHY BINARY PASS / FAIL INSTEAD OF 1-5 SCORES
A 1-5 score hides what went wrong and drifts between graders. PASS/FAIL per failure mode, with a quoted reason, is reproducible and tells engineers exactly what to fix.
1. Export 100 recent traces into a sheet; add a 'what went wrong' column.
2. Group notes into 5-8 named failure modes; count them.
3. Write one binary judge for the top mode; validate on 40 hand-labeled traces.
Counts are an example run (90 failing + 10 passing traces); the method is the point.
